A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with the same central framework and corresponding Appendices A–E. Text, equations, figures, and implementation tables are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original diagonal-network simulations, ResNet experiments on CIFAR-100, and representation analyses in Figures 3–4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds imperfect-pretraining simulations, SVHN transfer, optimizer/split experiments, and Transformer modular-arithmetic results.

M1.justification: The diagonal-network architecture, two-stage training, pathway rebalancing, readout reinitialization, and implicit penalty remain unchanged. Equations (2)–(3) are rewritten equivalently under symmetric initialization. The additional architectures and optimizer variants extend evaluation of the existing scaling interventions.

E1.justification: v2 expands beyond synthetic regression and CIFAR-100 to CIFAR-100-to-SVHN transfer and Transformer modular-arithmetic tasks with seen, shared-prime, and novel-prime moduli (Appendices D.5 and D.8). The arithmetic coverage is clearly new, although D.8 says addition while Figure 12 says multiplication.

E2.justification: Figure 11a introduces single-task ResNet baselines into the SVHN transfer comparison; v1's ResNet plots compare initialization scales without this baseline. Single-task diagonal-network experiments and the Lippl–Lindsey fine-tuning rescaling comparison were already documented, so the comparator expansion is limited.

E3.justification: New protocols include pretraining data scales below one, an additional CIFAR-100 60/40 class split, and Adam with pretraining weight decay and fine-tuning decay toward initial weights. Transformer evaluation introduces six pretraining targets, nine fine-tuning moduli, and specified training budgets. These supplement the retained protocols rather than establish reruns of existing experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds sensitivity to imperfect pretraining, a reduced-task-similarity probe using SVHN, optimizer and class-split robustness checks, and arithmetic-transfer comparisons organized by shared prime factors (Figures 4, 11–12). The original initialization sweeps and PR/ENSD representation analyses remain present.

E5.justification: Figure 12 specifies a new 25-seed protocol with one-standard-error bars for the Transformer experiments. Existing diagonal-network and ResNet run counts, Figure 3's two-standard-error reporting, and Appendix E's Monte Carlo uncertainty procedures are retained; additional runs of the original experiments are not established.

E6.justification: Figures 4, 11, and 12 add results on pretraining-strength dependence, SVHN transfer versus single-task learning, scaling effects under Adam and a 60/40 split, and higher errors for modular tasks involving novel prime factors. Original result plots are retained unchanged, including v1 Figure 4 as v2 Figure 5. These are additional results under new conditions.

T1.justification: The central theorems, propositions, and derivations are retained, while Sections 3.3 and 5.3 explicitly extend analysis to imperfect pretraining. Appendix C.1 removes the detailed assumptions concerning deterministic limits, interchange of limits, and analytic continuation, retaining only a generic replica-assumption qualification.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list broaden empirical applicability from CIFAR-100 ResNets to SVHN and Transformer arithmetic tasks. The contribution list also adds an explicit novelty claim for the integrated PT+FT characterization. The central four-regime theory and initialization-dependent generalization claims remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 explains why weak pretraining reduces sensitivity to relative scale and why imperfectly learned features can benefit from refinement even under full task overlap. It also interprets SVHN as a lower-overlap proxy and suggests optimizer dynamics may explain nonmonotonic scaling effects. Most existing architectural and uncontrolled-overlap limitations move into Section 6.

D1.justification: Appendix D.8 adds Transformer optimizer settings, one-million-step pretraining and 32,000-step fine-tuning budgets, embedding-scaling instructions, and the source codebase used. Figure 11 supplies Adam regularization details. Existing Appendix E implementation information remains largely unchanged, while the addition-versus-multiplication inconsistency limits reproducibility of the new arithmetic experiment.

R1.justification: v2 adds Jarvis et al. (2025), makes the integrated-characterization novelty claim explicit, and expands the explanation connecting diagonal-network dynamics to nonlinear networks. The positioning relative to Lippl and Lindsey remains substantially unchanged. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for retained works.

P1.justification: The overall section and appendix organization is retained. v2 reorganizes related-work paragraphs, expands replica-method and architectural explanations, brings representation analysis and limitations into Section 6, and revises the conclusion and publication front matter. Most existing exposition and proof text remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1 into separate training, teacher-task, and parameter panels and adds substantial multipanel displays for imperfect pretraining, ResNet robustness, and Transformer transfer (Figures 4, 11–12). Retained figures are relocated or renumbered, and the Appendix A plot is reformatted with a side caption.

improvement.justification: The new imperfect-pretraining, SVHN, optimizer/split, and Transformer experiments strengthen empirical support beyond v1's narrower validation. The central theory and original results remain intact. However, Appendix D.8 and Figure 12 disagree about the arithmetic fine-tuning task, and Appendix C loses explicit replica assumptions. These reporting weaknesses limit the overall gain despite the useful additional evidence.
